I changed `BlockManager.fast_xs` in `pandas/core/internals/managers.py`. It now copies the row when the single block's data is shared with nothing else. I haven't run or tested it.

**Cause:** selecting a row and a non-adjacent list of columns first copies the columns into a temporary 3 by N block. The row was then taken as a view of that block, so the 3-value result kept the whole temporary alive.

**Fix:** if `refs.has_reference()` is false, the block has no other users, so it is either a temporary or data nobody else holds. In that case `fast_xs` now builds the row from `result.copy()` and gives it no shared refs. When the data is shared, it still returns a view tracked by the refs, as before.

**Side effect:** `df.iloc[0]` on a single-block DataFrame that has no other references to its data now also returns a copy. That copy is only one value per column. Copy-on-write already makes a later write to either side trigger a copy, so the visible behaviour shouldn't change.

I didn't add a test.
